title: Open immersions of spaces descend along etale target covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:X\to P$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{P_i\to P\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale maps with each $P_i$ a scheme. Suppose each base change $X\times_PP_i\to P_i$ is an open immersion, meaning it is represented by the inclusion of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $a$ is representable and is an open immersion: for every scheme $V\to P$, $X\times_PV$ is a scheme and its projection to $V$ is an open immersion. In particular, if $P$ is a scheme then $X$ is a scheme isomorphic over $P$ to an open subscheme of $P$.

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), open-immersion case, (4) implies (1) and (1) implies (2); also spaces-descent.tex Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ with a map $t:h_T\to P$. Put $F=h_T\times_P X$, as a sheaf-valued fibre product, without assuming it is a scheme. For each $i$ put $T_i=T\times_P P_i$. Because $P_i\to P$ is representable etale, $T_i$ is a scheme and $q_i:T_i\to T$ is etale by the scheme-test definition. The jointly surjective family in the hypothesis remains jointly surjective on this scheme test: the family of base-change projections $q_i$ covers $T$. This is the covering meaning of jointly surjective representable etale maps; all products here are the actual sheaf fibre products. Scheme products used below are the chosen products of [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 041X, proof, applied after an arbitrary scheme test; scheme-test definition of representable etale covers

proof.text: Regard the $T_i$ as objects of $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $(q_i)$ as a covering of its identity object. The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] gives an fpqc covering of $T$, with no finiteness assumption on $I$ or quasi-compactness assumption on the $T_i$. Also $(q_i)$ is an fppf covering: etale means flat and locally of finite presentation, and it is jointly surjective. For any scheme $Z\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] gives the jointly surjective etale family $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i\to Z$; by the same definitions this too is fppf. We will use these fppf covers for the sheaf condition, not assume that an algebraic space is an fpqc sheaf.

Write $Y_i=X\times_P P_i$, a scheme whose projection $j_i:Y_i\to P_i$ is an open immersion by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], the scheme $Y_i\times_{P_i}T_i\to T_i$ is an open immersion. Denote its image open subscheme by $W_i\subset T_i$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $h_{W_i}$ over $h_{T_i}$ with $F\times_{h_T}h_{T_i}$. For $R_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$, the two pullbacks of these open subschemes are open by the same base-change lemma, and both represent the identical subfunctor $F\times_{h_T}h_{R_{ij}}$ of $h_{R_{ij}}$. They are therefore equal as opens of $R_{ij}$: membership of a point $r$ in either open is exactly the factorization of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(r)\to R_{ij}$ through that subfunctor. Their structure sheaves are both restrictions of $\mathcal O_{R_{ij}}$.

source.place: Tag 041X, proof: the two pullbacks of the open subscheme are equal

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] to the fpqc covering $(q_i:T_i\to T)$ from Step 2 and the compatible opens $W_i$ from Step 3. It gives a unique open subscheme $U\subset T$ such that $U\times_TT_i=W_i$ for every $i$. Thus the descended object is an actual open subscheme of the arbitrary test scheme $T$. This lemma descends only open subsets of schemes; identification with $F$ is still to be proved.

The identifications of Step 3 give sections $b_i\in X(W_i)$, the maps $W_i\simeq Y_i\times_{P_i}T_i\to X$. On $W_i\times_UW_j$ they agree: after mapping to $R_{ij}$, both are the unique $X$-section corresponding to the inclusion of the same open in the common subfunctor of Step 3. The family $W_i=U\times_TT_i\to U$ is fppf by Step 2. Since $X$ is an fppf sheaf, its equalizer condition glues the $b_i$ to a unique $b\in X(U)$. Moreover $a(b)$ equals the image in $P(U)$ of $U\hookrightarrow T\xrightarrow{t}P$: they agree after restriction to every $W_i$, and $P$ is an fppf sheaf too. Consequently $b$ defines a map $h_U\to F$ over $h_T$, by pullback of this section.

source.place: Tag 041X, proof: glue the compatible local maps from the descended open into X; here the etale covers permit the defining fppf sheaf condition

proof.text: For every scheme $g:Z\to T$ and $x\in F(Z)$, pull back along the fppf covering $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i\to Z$. The identification $F|_{T_i}=h_{W_i}$ gives a unique map $Z_i\to W_i$. Since $W_i=q_i^{-1}(U)$, the structural map $Z_i\to Z\xrightarrow{g}T$ has image in $U$. Joint surjectivity of $(Z_i\to Z)$ forces $g(Z)\subset U$. Restricting the continuous map and sheaf map of $g$ to this open gives a unique scheme morphism $\widetilde g:Z\to U$ with $g$ equal to its composite with $U\hookrightarrow T$. On every $Z_i$, the sections $x$ and $\widetilde g^*b$ agree, since each is the unique element over the fixed $Z_i\to T_i$ in the represented open $W_i$. Separatedness in the defining sheaf condition for $X$ gives $x=\widetilde g^*b$. Conversely every $Z\to U$ gives such an $x$ by pulling back $b$. Uniqueness of the factorization through an open shows that these constructions are inverse. The covers used here are exactly those supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change].

source.place: Tag 041X, final paragraph: factor every test point through the descended open and show the resulting map of sheaves is bijective

proof.text: The bijections of Step 6 commute with pullback in $Z$: the forward map is pullback of $b$, and its inverse is the unique factorization through $U$. They therefore identify $F=h_T\times_PX$ with $h_U$, with its projection to $h_T$ equal to the open inclusion $U\hookrightarrow T$. Since $T\to P$ was arbitrary, the scheme-test definition of representability proves that $a$ is representable, and every scheme-test projection is an open immersion. This is precisely the asserted meaning of an open immersion of algebraic spaces. If $P$ is itself a scheme, take $T=P$ and $t$ the identity to obtain $X\simeq U\subset P$.

source.place: Tag 03M4, conditions (1) and (2); these are now verified by the constructed open on each scheme test

proof_origin.place: Tag 041X, lemma-descending-property-open-immersion, proof by descent of compatible opens (03N0) and the sheaf condition. Apply this construction directly to each scheme test and its given etale family; all sheaf gluing uses fppf covers, so no fpqc-sheaf theorem is needed.

lean.statement: theorem isOpenImmersion_of_etale_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} {X P : AlgebraicSpace S} (a : X ⟶ P) (I : Type u) (P_i : I → Over S) (p_i : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (P_i i) ⟶ P.obj.obj) (h_etale : ∀ i, IsEtale (p_i i)) (h_joint : ∀ (T : Over S) (x : P.obj.obj.obj (Opposite.op T)), ∃ (R : Sieve T.left), R ∈ Scheme.fppfTopology T.left ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T), R f.left → ∃ (i : I) (y : (yoneda.obj (P_i i)).obj (Opposite.op U)), (p_i i).app (Opposite.op U) y = P.obj.obj.map f.op x) (h_open : ∀ i, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q => IsOpenImmersion q.left) (pullback.snd a.hom.hom (p_i i))) : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q => IsOpenImmersion q.left) a.hom.hom
